method: Reviewed the lesson against OWASP Transaction Authorization and OWASP LLM06:2025 Excessive Agency guidance. Compiled all embedded Python blocks, ran the deterministic local approval-policy simulation, and asserted its counts and evidence boundaries. No provider or external service calls were made.

observations.trace: The fixture reproduced A 7/0/0, B 2/0/0, C 1/0/1, and D 0/1/2 pre-action approvals/post-reviews/unapproved risk actions; D review occurs after effects and cannot prevent them. These are deterministic counts from author-assigned labels, not evidence about human fatigue, approval quality, risk severity, or universal policy superiority. The lesson now marks pseudo-code limits, authorization, immutable proposal binding, reapproval after edits, atomic lifecycle and unknown external outcomes.

limitations: The policy counts are a deterministic synthetic fixture; they do not measure real user fatigue, review quality, risk severity, or the optimal approval policy.
The pseudo-code is an architectural sketch, not an implementation proving complete path coverage, concurrency safety, authorization correctness, or exactly-once external effects.
No production authorization system, identity provider, external action, or human approval workflow was tested.
